original_statement: Adaptive LQR achieves up to 12.5% ± 2.1% improvement in energy efficiency vs fixed-gain LQR (abstract, L9).
required_evidence: A defined metric, cycle, SoH and statistic; saved runs of both controllers on the same plant; the improvement recomputed from them.
implemented_experiment: Pre-registered primary experiment (S1/S2 x SoH 1.0-0.7), gamma sweep S-B, fixed-gain family S-C, paired robustness S-D, energy decomposition.
contradictory_or_negative_evidence: Primary (S1, SoH 0.8): dE = +0.003 % (scheduled uses slightly MORE energy), RMSE ratio 1.011 -> NO PRACTICAL DIFFERENCE. All 8 pairs |dE| <= 0.005 %; all 15 gamma settings |dE| <= 0.04 %; S-D mean -0.054 % [95 % bootstrap -0.058, -0.050]. Battery resistive losses were 1.1-2.1 % of supplied energy in the tested runs, which explains the small tested differences; this is not a bound on what other controllers or a more complete plant could achieve (corrected 2026-10-24). Report body (L5468-5472) itself implies 10.2 %, not 12.5 %. The ± interval was added editorially (D:\EUREKA\AUDIT_REPORT.md L28, L195).
final_reporting_recommendation: Withdraw. Report instead: "In a documented simulation model, SoH scheduling of LQR weights changed model-computed energy per km by less than 0.06 %" with the conditions of N01-N03. The original conditions are undefined, so the contradiction holds for this documented model, not for an unspecified one.

original_statement: 15.3% ± 2.8% reduction in battery capacity fade over 1000 operational cycles (abstract, L9).
required_evidence: An ageing model with documented LFP parameter provenance, validated against measured cycling data; simulated lifetime runs of both controllers.
contradictory_or_negative_evidence: Report gives 15.3 % (abstract) and 14 % (L5480) for the same quantity (CHK-FADE-PCT); fade figure spans 1500 cycles and is drawn from hard-coded curves (C36, C40). Current-related metrics differ negligibly between controllers (peak current 274.794 vs 274.793 A).
final_reporting_recommendation: Withdraw. No capacity-fade claim of any size is supported; a real-battery claim would additionally REQUIRE_PHYSICAL_VALIDATION.

Huria, M. Ceraolo, J. Gazzarri, R. Jackey, "High fidelity electrical model with thermal dependence for characterization and simulation of high power lithium battery cells", 2012 IEEE International Electric Vehicle Conference (IEVC), pp. 1-8, doi:10.1109/IEVC.2012.6183271, not IEEE Trans. Its abstract describes a one-RC equivalent-circuit model identified on LiNiCoMnO2 (NMC)/graphite cells, with no ageing or SEI model; it therefore supports neither LFP-specific parameters (report Assumption 5, L750, not a registered location of this claim) nor the SEI ageing model (L5998).

original_statement: NEW. On the documented 48 V micro-EV model (flat road, synthetic profiles S1/S2 up to 50 km/h, SoH 70-100 %, SoH known), the report's SoH-scheduled LQR (gamma = 1) changes model-computed battery energy per km by +0.000 to +0.005 % relative to fixed-gain LQR, with 0.4-2.0 % higher tracking RMSE: no practical difference (pre-registered ±1 % margin).
required_evidence: Pre-registered primary experiment, verification gate, regenerable outputs.
contradictory_or_negative_evidence: With velocity-measurement noise (S-D) the sign flips (-0.054 %), still far inside the margin. Traction limit and friction brake were essentially never active on S1/S2, so actuator-constrained behaviour is untested.
final_reporting_recommendation: Report with all conditions; do not generalise to real vehicles, standard cycles, grades or efficiency maps.

original_statement: NEW. In the same model a single, non-scheduled fixed-gain LQR (R scaled by 0.1) gives lower SoH-averaged energy (49.854 vs 49.881 Wh/km) and lower SoH-averaged RMSE (0.038 vs 0.051 m/s) than the scheduled controller; the competing hypothesis H_C holds.
implemented_experiment: S-C fixed-gain family (41 members x 4 SoH).
contradictory_or_negative_evidence: The best member lies at the edge of the pre-registered family (0.1x), so the optimum may be outside the tested range; the family spans only 0.28 % in energy.
final_reporting_recommendation: Report as: SoH scheduling of weights did not outperform retuning a single fixed gain in this model.

original_statement: NEW. Over 50 paired draws from ASSUMED uniform parameter ranges with velocity noise (S1, SoH 0.8), mean dE = -0.054 % (bootstrap 95 % [-0.058, -0.050] for the Monte Carlo mean); every draw within ±1 %; no tracking failures.
contradictory_or_negative_evidence: Distributions are assumed, not measured; the interval is not an inference about vehicles.
final_reporting_recommendation: Report with the interpretation limit; no p-values.

original_statement: NEW. In this model, battery resistive losses are 1.1-2.1 % of supplied energy on S1/S2 in the tested runs; this is the energy share that SoH changes directly. It explains the tested null result and is not a bound on what other controllers could save.
contradictory_or_negative_evidence: Constant motor/inverter efficiency hides any part-load efficiency effect of control; a measured efficiency map could enlarge the controllable share. 2026-10-24: energy can also differ between controllers through motor/inverter and gear loss asymmetry (motoring vs regeneration), R1 loss, regenerated energy, friction braking and tracking deviations; no bound over all controllers has been derived.
final_reporting_recommendation: Report as a model-specific energy decomposition of the tested runs, not as a bound; name the efficiency-map limitation.
